evidence.note: The film is based on George du Maurier's novel Trilby. Wikipedia says it was serialized in Harper's New Monthly Magazine from January to August 1894 and published in book form on 8 September 1894. A work published in 1894 has passed its US copyright term (year+76, 1970 at the latest), so the source novel is in the public domain in the US.

watch.label: Svengali (1931), Archie Mayo, with John Barrymore and Marian Marsh

editorial:
Svengali is Warner Bros.' 1931 adaptation of George du Maurier's 1894 novel Trilby. Archie Mayo directed it and Barney McGill shot it. John Barrymore plays the hypnotist who turns Trilby (Marian Marsh) into a singer. The cast also includes Bramwell Fletcher, Donald Crisp and Carmel Myers. It opened in New York on 1 May 1931. Wikipedia, citing the AFI Catalog, gives the shoot as 12 January to 21 February 1931. A creator might want it for Barrymore's performance.

The print's rights status is not confirmed. The renewal window for a 1931 film ran mainly in 1958, with 1959 as a late margin. Only the opening part of the OCR text of each of those two Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes was read, and it showed no renewal. That is not a full search, so check the full volumes and the Copyright Office records yourself before treating the film as free. The source novel is out of copyright by term. The score and track were not traced to a composer, so check any music before you lift the audio. Check each upload for added material, and take the picture from a plain scan.
faq: Is the 1931 Svengali free to use in the US?

Not confirmed. The source novel Trilby (1894) is out of copyright by term. For the film, the 1958 and 1959 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes were only partly read, and the part read showed no renewal. Search the full volumes and the Copyright Office records to finish the check. The score and recorded music were not traced, and no trademark check was done.
Can I use the Internet Archive copies as they are?
Check each upload first. The quality and any added material, such as subtitles or edits, were not checked. Use a plain scan and check the rights in any added material.
